images.what_i_saw: Wide coastal shot: hills framing King George Sound, a surfer riding a peeling wave, an anchored bulk carrier offshore. No structure visible (reef is fully submerged, crest -1.0 m AHD), but same article/background as image 2 which ABC explicitly captions as the reef wave.
Beach-level shot through dune grass: clean left-breaking wave peeling, surfer visible, same hills/ship background. ABC's own caption reads 'A clean wave breaks on the Albany surf reef.'

Aerial/drone shot: dredge/crane barge working directly over a submerged elongated dark rock-berm shape in turquoise water, matching the ~165 m reef footprint. ABC caption: 'Specialised vessels came from around the world to build the Albany surf reef.'

Surfer bottom-turning on a breaking wave, whitewater peeling left. No structure visible (expected, reef submerged). Hosted on Raised Water Research's dedicated Midds Reef spot page, whose sole subject is this reef break, though no explicit on-image caption names the reef.

Aerial shot: sandy beach, shallow turquoise water, clear elongated dark submerged rock-berm shadow with a small dredge vessel alongside. Embedded EXIF description: 'An aerial shot of the Great Southern's artificial surf reef under construction in May, 2025.'

Official Bluecoast Consulting Engineers design table and plan-view diagram (not a photo): shows crest length 110 m, offshore distance 140 m, left-hander orientation, 41% surfability target, position 350 m north of Big4 caravan park. A diagram of the structure's shape/position, not a photograph of built rock.
